verdict.rationale: Bruno stores collections, including their pre/post-request scripts and tests, as plain-text Bru files on the filesystem, and its docs say this is designed so you can version them with Git and review changes like code. It also ships a built-in Git UI (init, diff, pull, commit) and documents a terminal Git workflow, and community users confirm the plain-text-in-Git benefit. Missing for 10: explicit documented rollback/revert of automations within Bruno (implied only through standard Git), and specific coverage of reviewing script or automation changes beyond general diffs.
